summary: Iteration 92 — Super Admin management (workspaces, users, invites, guardrails, regression). Backend: 12 passed + 1 xfailed (documented bug) via pytest. Web UI end-to-end verified via Playwright: all 4 tabs render (sa-tab-settings/workspaces/users/invites), Add-user modal creates a user (must_change_password=true, can login), toggle super-admin adds SUPER badge, reset password modal works, suspend adds SUSPENDED badge, delete removes the row, credits editor opens with sa-ws-monthly-{id}/sa-ws-topup-{id}, plan dropdown renders 100 workspace rows with sa-ws-plan-{id}. Invites tab generates codes and lists recent invites with sa-invite-copy-{code}. All guardrails (self-suspend / self-revoke-super / self-delete) return 400. One-time top-up regression works on non-free plans (750=500+250 style). BUG FOUND: workspace suspension does not cascade to workspace_members.status, so suspended workspace owners still get 200 on /api/auth/me.

critical.issue: Suspension updates workspaces.status and users.status but does NOT update workspace_members.status. In get_user(), the workspace_members overlay sets user.status back to 'active' (line ~127 of deps.py), so suspended workspace owners still pass require_user and get 200 on /api/auth/me. The point of workspace suspension (blocking members) is defeated. Fix: mirror status onto workspace_members like the /users PATCH does.

minor.issue: For free-plan workspaces, credits_remaining is capped to the plan's monthly allowance (billing.py:399 `cap = monthly if plan.id == 'free'`). One-time top-up therefore has NO observable effect on credits_remaining until the plan is switched to pro/team (or monthly is raised via override). credits_total also shows the capped value, so admins get no UI signal that the top-up was applied. Consider surfacing 'extra_credits' separately or exempting extra credits from the free-plan cap.

issues: Plan <select> uses browser's native dropdown instead of the shadcn Select component used elsewhere in the app — inconsistent styling. Low priority.

Row for the current super admin (amit@demo.team) shows suspend/delete/revoke-super buttons enabled, even though the backend refuses (400). Consider disabling these buttons or hiding them for the row where u.id === current user id to avoid a dead-click UX.

action_items: HIGH — Cascade workspace suspension to workspace_members.status in PATCH /api/superadmin/workspaces/{ws_id} (mirror the /users PATCH which already updates workspace_members). Otherwise workspace suspension is a no-op for owner/member access.

MEDIUM — In UI, disable/hide sa-user-suspend-{me}, sa-user-super-{me}, sa-user-delete-{me} buttons where the row is the current super admin — the backend already 400s but UX shows an interactive control.
LOW — In services/billing.py get_usage(), decide whether extra_credits should be exempt from the free-plan monthly cap. Currently a one-time top-up is silently swallowed for free-plan workspaces.

This is the core RCA of the workspace-suspend bug.

backend/routes/superadmin.py:283 — After insert, ensure_membership() is called with role but not with an explicit status. This is OK for new users, but confirms the assumption that membership.status defaults to 'active' and will always mask a workspace-level suspension.
InvitesTab.jsx doesn't validate the count input server-side result — a user could type 999 in the number box; backend clamps to 25 silently. Consider adding max=25 hint in UI toast.

rca of the issue: Workspace-suspend no-op RCA: PATCH /api/superadmin/workspaces/{id} (backend/routes/superadmin.py:169-180) sets workspaces.status='suspended' and users.status='suspended' but omits workspace_members.status. In deps.get_user() (line 122-128), for any user whose active workspace has a workspace_members row, `user['status']` is unconditionally overlaid from `m.get('status')` — the membership row still says 'active', so the raw users.status='suspended' is masked. require_user() (line 135) then sees 'active' and allows the request. Reproduction: 1) POST /api/superadmin/users to create a fresh user (returns uid + ws_id). 2) Login as that user in a separate session — /api/auth/me returns 200. 3) As super admin, PATCH /api/superadmin/workspaces/{ws_id} {suspended:true}. 4) In the user session, GET /api/auth/me — expected 403, actual 200. Fix: add `await db.workspace_members.update_many({'workspace_id': ws_id, 'status': {'$ne': 'removed'}}, {'$set': {'status': new_status}})` alongside the existing users.update_many call.
